$comment: Files in src/app allowed to differ from apps/web/src (or to have no web counterpart). One entry per file or glob, relative to src/app. category: platform (a platform service is the reason), native-editor (the native editor is), desktop-only (a screen or tool web has no counterpart for). reason: why, in a sentence. Kit-API drift (onPress, testID, lists, dialogs) is never a reason: phase 4 removes it.

entries.reason: Assets (icons, illustrations, SVG and raster images) generated by tools/gen-assets.mjs, since the GPUI host cannot import asset files the way web's Vite build does.
Smoke screen that exercises every @platform service on the native host; web has no such screen.
Standalone status screen root.tsx shows for the boot/demo mode of the native host; web has no such screen.
Developer benchmarks for the native host (attachment I/O), not part of the app.
Actions the native editor asks its host for (links, attachments, previews); Tiptap does these inside the web editor.
Binds the native editor's host actions to the app's stores and attachment helpers; web's Tiptap editor has no host bridge.

The bug report link opens with the shell service (shell.openUrl); web calls window.open, which the desktop host does not have. The error list also keeps the selectable class so a bug report can copy it: the old desktop code selected it, and web's text is not selectable (app.css only enables selection for the selectable class).
The password field's widest width is 400 where web writes max(30%, 400px): the desktop layout has no CSS min()/max(). Otherwise identical to web.
The filter input is styled through Field's styles.input where web reaches it with an `input` selector in sx: desktop has no stylesheet selectors. Otherwise identical to web.

Web draws PDFs with @react-pdf-viewer (DOM, canvas and its stylesheet); desktop draws them with the kit's PDF viewer over @react-native-gpui/pdf and saves, copies and prints through @platform files, shell and window services.
Web's lightbox is a DOM image viewer that adds a class to document.body and listens for keys on document; desktop draws the image with kit primitives and takes keys from the kit and the window.

Web scrolls the two versions together with react-scroll-sync over DOM scroll containers and renders diffblazer's HTML; desktop has no DOM, so it syncs the kit's scroll views and draws the diff from text.

Web listens for window error and unhandledrejection events, removes the #splash element and reloads with window.location; desktop takes errors from the Hermes runtime and restarts through the lifecycle service.
Web's title bar calls the Electron bridge and window.close; desktop's window controls are the windowControls platform service and the kit's native TitleBar.
Web writes the theme into a <style> element, a theme-color <meta> and the <html> element; desktop has no document and hands the theme to the kit's ThemeScope.
Web picks files with react-dropzone and hashes them with hash-wasm (WebAssembly); desktop picks files with the files platform service and hashes with the crypto service's xxh64.

Web hashes with hash-wasm (WebAssembly) and writes the log with /
and the help link with ; desktop hashes with the crypto service and draws the log as text and the link with the kit.
Web uses a raw <select> and an <a> link; desktop has no HTML elements and uses the kit's Select and a link Text.
Desktop's xxh64 from the crypto platform service, which stands in for hash-wasm (WebAssembly) that the importer uses on web.
Web draws the loading skeleton with react-loading-skeleton (DOM and CSS animation); desktop draws it with kit boxes.
Web lays the calendar out with CSS grid (display: grid) and @rehookify/datepicker; desktop lays out with flexbox only, so the calendar is built from rows.
Web imports the empty-list illustrations as .svg files through Vite; the desktop host cannot import asset files and draws the generated illustrations (illustrations.generated.ts).
Web's icons import @mdi/react and .svg?react files through Vite; desktop draws the same glyphs from the generated paths in icons.generated.ts through the kit's Icon.
Makes the generated desktop icons (see icons.ts); web builds its icons from @mdi/react and SVG components.
Web asks "don't show again" with the synchronous window.confirm; desktop has no blocking browser dialog and asks with ConfirmDialog.
Web takes a pasted code from the input's paste event; the desktop text field raises no paste event, so a pasted code arrives through onChange and is split there.
Web lays action buttons out with CSS grid and opens links with window.open/window.location; desktop lays out with flexbox and opens links with the shell service.
Web shows each bar's tooltip with CSS child selectors (&:hover .tooltip, &:hover .bar) and CSS transition strings; desktop has no stylesheet selectors and uses the kit's hover state on each bar.
Web sizes the switch's label with a `& label` selector; desktop has no stylesheet selectors and styles the label itself.
Web places the background art with CSS grid (justifySelf) and transformOrigin; desktop lays out with flexbox and its transforms always use the element's centre.
Draws the generated SVG and raster assets with the theme's colours; web shows the same files with through Vite, which the desktop host cannot import.
Shows the native window once the first screen has drawn (or after a timeout); a browser tab has no window to reveal.

Web reveals each notebook's add button with CSS child selectors (&:hover .add-sub-notebook, &:focus-within) and styles the list with listStyle; desktop has no stylesheet selectors or list markers and uses the kit's group hover.

Draws its own backdrop and closes on a click there. Web's dialog reads react-modal's DOM (contentEl and offsetLeft/clientWidth geometry) and closes on a mousedown outside that element; the desktop kit's Modal does not expose those, so the close and the layout stay in the desktop file.

Desktop rows are flex layouts, not web's table rows. Attachments are read as base64 (downloadAttachment with base64) and PDFs open as base64 data URLs, because the desktop host has no Blob URLs (web uses URL.createObjectURL). The context menu opens at the pointer through the desktop menu hook.

Keeps the publish form in local state with its own validation and opens the link with shell.openUrl. Web binds the fields with react-hook-form register(), which reads DOM inputs; desktop inputs are native elements, and web's target=_blank anchor has no desktop equivalent.

Uses the desktop ThemeScope in place of web's ScopedThemeProvider and the kit's theme-token colours in place of var(--icon-error). The status icons spin with the kit's rotate prop, and web's responsive display arrays are not drawn.

The spell-check item is not gated on IS_DESKTOP_APP, because the desktop has its own spell checker service. The item gap is a constant rather than a theme lookup, and the list uses the kit's containerSx and placeholderSx props. The collapse caret rotates as on web.

The desktop kit has no alpha() from @theme-ui/color and no CSS hover or transition, so the accent tint comes from a hex colour helper that accepts only #rrggbb and falls back to background-secondary for anything else. The size is split into width and height.

Draws the single-line label with the kit's lineClamp in place of web's CSS ellipsis, and the dismiss control with the kit's secondary button variant. Adds a chip prop with a group-hover background, takes container styles as containerSx, and has no className.

onToggle gets the ctrl or meta state as a boolean, where web passes the DOM event. The label is the element's title, and the unchecked hover colour is the uncheckedGroupHoverColor prop instead of web's CSS class.
onClick gets the ctrl or meta state as a boolean, not the DOM event. The deprecated onPress alias still works, and the click stops at the remove icon.

Renders the desktop MenuHost, which draws the menu panel in the app. Web's wrapper hands the menu to the native shell when it can (use-menu.ts isNative), and the desktop host has no showMenu call, so the menu always draws in the app.

The desktop host for the in-app menu panel. It connects the kit's desktop menu presenter to the menu store and to the @platform keyboard service. Web has no such file: its MenuPresenter is wired in global-menu-wrapper.
Re-exports the kit's shared menu store, which positions the menu from an anchor rectangle, because the desktop kit measures native elements. Web's use-menu store keys the menu on a target element.

Desktop's own lock screen. It unlocks with the native keychain through @platform safeStorage and with WebAuthn security keys through the platform service. Web's lock UI is inline in views/app-lock.tsx and uses the web key store's desktop.safeStorage bridge.
apps/web's split pane is a DOM implementation (CSS class names, window mousemove/mouseup listeners, document.body classList); desktop re-exports the kit's SplitPane and Pane, which resize natively.

apps/web virtualizes with @tanstack/react-virtual on the DOM scroll element it finds with closest('.ms-container') and positions rows with CSS transforms; desktop draws the same list with the kit's Virtuoso on the native list.
apps/web virtualizes with @tanstack/react-virtual on the DOM scroll element it finds with closest('.ms-container'); desktop lays the grid out in rows on the kit's Virtuoso.
apps/web measures its DOM scroll container (closest('.ms-container')) for @tanstack/react-virtual; desktop uses the kit's TableVirtuoso, which owns its native scroll view.

apps/web renders each row in a raw <div> with onMouseUp and finds rows with document.getElementById to focus or click them (waitForElement); desktop has no DOM, so rows register an opener and the focused index with the list instead.

apps/web renders raw <div> items and skeletons, finds items with document.querySelector/getElementById (reveal flash with classList, waitForElement focus and click); desktop has no DOM, so items register with a selection context (list-container/selection.ts) instead.
Desktop-only stand-in for the DOM focus and click that apps/web's list uses (document.getElementById(...).focus()/click()): items register their open action and read the focused index.
apps/web reorders the sidebar with @dnd-kit (DOM pointer sensors and CSS transforms); desktop reorders with the kit's SortableList.
apps/web's SortableNavigationItem is built on @dnd-kit/sortable (DOM); desktop has no such item, the kit's SortableList moves the rows.
